audit_status.source_base: Greek Acts text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Corinth, Priscilla/Aquila, tentmaking, synagogue opposition, Crispus, vision, Gallio, Cenchreae, Ephesus, Apollos instructed more accurately.

verses.restored: After these things, departing from Athens, he came to Corinth.

familiar.text: After these things Paul departed from Athens, and came to Corinth;

modern.text: After this, Paul left Athens and went to Corinth.

original.text: ⸀Μετὰ ταῦτα ⸀χωρισθεὶς ἐκ τῶν Ἀθηνῶν ἦλθεν εἰς Κόρινθον.

verses.restored: He found a certain Judean named Aquila, Pontian by birth, recently come from Italy with Priscilla his wife, because Claudius had ordered all the Judeans to depart from Rome; he came to them.

familiar.text: And found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, lately come from Italy, with his wife Priscilla; (because that Claudius had commanded all Jews to depart from Rome:) and came unto them.

modern.text: There he found a Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla because Claudius had ordered all the Jews to leave Rome. Paul went to visit them,

original.text: καὶ εὑρών τινα Ἰουδαῖον ὀνόματι Ἀκύλαν, Ποντικὸν τῷ γένει, προσφάτως ἐληλυθότα ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰταλίας καὶ Πρίσκιλλαν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ διὰ τὸ ⸀διατεταχέναι Κλαύδιον χωρίζεσθαι πάντας τοὺς Ἰουδαίους ⸀ἀπὸ τῆς Ῥώμης, προσῆλθεν αὐτοῖς,

verses.restored: Because he was of the same trade, he remained with them and worked; for by trade they were tentmakers.

familiar.text: And because he was of the same craft, he abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers.

modern.text: and he stayed and worked with them because they were tentmakers by trade, just as he was.

original.text: καὶ διὰ τὸ ὁμότεχνον εἶναι ἔμενεν παρʼ αὐτοῖς καὶ ⸀ἠργάζετο, ἦσαν γὰρ σκηνοποιοὶ ⸂τῇ τέχνῃ⸃.

verses.restored: He was reasoning in the synagogue every Sabbath and persuading Judeans and Greeks.

familiar.text: And he reasoned in the synagogue every sabbath, and persuaded the Jews and the Greeks.

modern.text: Every Sabbath he reasoned in the synagogue, trying to persuade Jews and Greeks alike.

original.text: διελέγετο δὲ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ κατὰ πᾶν σάββατον, ἔπειθέν τε Ἰουδαίους καὶ Ἕλληνας.

verses.restored: When Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul was pressed by the word, testifying to the Judeans that Jesus is the Messiah.

familiar.text: And when Silas and Timotheus were come from Macedonia, Paul was pressed in the spirit, and testified to the Jews that Jesus was Christ.

modern.text: And when Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul devoted himself fully to the word, testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.

original.text: Ὡς δὲ κατῆλθον ἀπὸ τῆς Μακεδονίας ὅ τε Σιλᾶς καὶ ὁ Τιμόθεος, συνείχετο τῷ ⸀λόγῳ ὁ Παῦλος, διαμαρτυρόμενος τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ⸀εἶναι τὸν χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν.

verses.restored: When they opposed and blasphemed, he shook out his garments and said to them, Your blood be upon your head; I am clean. From now I will go to the nations.

familiar.text: And when they opposed themselves, and blasphemed, he shook his raiment, and said unto them, Your blood be upon your own heads; I am clean: from henceforth I will go unto the Gentiles.

modern.text: But when they opposed and insulted him, he shook out his garments and told them, “Your blood be on your own heads! I am innocent of it. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.”

original.text: ἀντιτασσομένων δὲ αὐτῶν καὶ βλασφημούντων ἐκτιναξάμενος τὰ ἱμάτια εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τὸ αἷμα ὑμῶν ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν ὑμῶν· καθαρὸς ἐγώ· ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν εἰς τὰ ἔθνη πορεύσομαι.

verses.restored: Departing from there, he entered the house of a certain Titius Justus, a reverer of the Divine, whose house was adjoining the synagogue.

familiar.text: And he departed thence, and entered into a certain man’s house, named Justus, one that worshipped God, whose house joined hard to the synagogue.

modern.text: So Paul left the synagogue and went next door to the house of Titus Justus, a worshiper of God.

original.text: καὶ μεταβὰς ἐκεῖθεν ⸀εἰσῆλθεν εἰς οἰκίαν τινὸς ὀνόματι ⸀Τιτίου Ἰούστου σεβομένου τὸν θεόν, οὗ ἡ οἰκία ἦν συνομοροῦσα τῇ συναγωγῇ.

verses.restored: Crispus, the synagogue ruler, trusted the Lord with his whole house, and many of the Corinthians hearing were trusting and being baptized.

familiar.text: And Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his house; and many of the Corinthians hearing believed, and were baptized.

modern.text: Crispus, the synagogue leader, and his whole household believed in the Lord. And many of the Corinthians who heard the message believed and were baptized.

original.text: Κρίσπος δὲ ὁ ἀρχισυνάγωγος ἐπίστευσεν τῷ κυρίῳ σὺν ὅλῳ τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ, καὶ πολλοὶ τῶν Κορινθίων ἀκούοντες ἐπίστευον καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο.

verses.restored: The Lord said to Paul through a vision in the night, Do not fear, but speak and do not be silent,

familiar.text: Then spake the Lord to Paul in the night by a vision, Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace:

modern.text: One night the Lord spoke to Paul in a vision: “Do not be afraid; keep on speaking; do not be silent.

original.text: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος ⸂ἐν νυκτὶ διʼ ὁράματος⸃ τῷ Παύλῳ· Μὴ φοβοῦ, ἀλλὰ λάλει καὶ μὴ σιωπήσῃς,

verses.restored: because I am with you, and no one will lay a hand on you to harm you, because there is much people for me in this city.

familiar.text: For I am with thee, and no man shall set on thee to hurt thee: for I have much people in this city.

modern.text: For I am with you and no one will lay a hand on you, because I have many people in this city.”

original.text: διότι ἐγώ εἰμι μετὰ σοῦ καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐπιθήσεταί σοι τοῦ κακῶσαί σε, διότι λαός ἐστί μοι πολὺς ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ.

verses.restored: He sat there a year and six months, teaching the word of the Divine among them.

familiar.text: And he continued there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.

modern.text: So Paul stayed for a year and a half, teaching the word of God among the Corinthians. Paul before Gallio

original.text: ἐκάθισεν ⸀δὲ ἐνιαυτὸν καὶ μῆνας ἓξ διδάσκων ἐν αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: But when Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Judeans rose with one accord against Paul and brought him to the judgment seat,

familiar.text: And when Gallio was the deputy of Achaia, the Jews made insurrection with one accord against Paul, and brought him to the judgment seat,

modern.text: While Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews coordinated an attack on Paul and brought him before the judgment seat.

original.text: Γαλλίωνος δὲ ⸂ἀνθυπάτου ὄντος⸃ τῆς Ἀχαΐας κατεπέστησαν ⸂ὁμοθυμαδὸν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι⸃ τῷ Παύλῳ καὶ ἤγαγον αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸ βῆμα,

verses.restored: saying, This one persuades humans to revere the Divine contrary to the Law.

familiar.text: Saying, This fellow persuadeth men to worship God contrary to the law.

modern.text: “This man is persuading the people to worship God in ways contrary to the law,” they said.

original.text: λέγοντες ὅτι Παρὰ τὸν νόμον ⸂ἀναπείθει οὗτος⸃ τοὺς ἀνθρώπους σέβεσθαι τὸν θεόν.

verses.restored: As Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Judeans, If indeed it were some wrongdoing or wicked crime, O Judeans, according to reason I would put up with you.

familiar.text: And when Paul was now about to open his mouth, Gallio said unto the Jews, If it were a matter of wrong or wicked lewdness, O ye Jews, reason would that I should bear with you:

modern.text: But just as Paul was about to speak, Gallio told the Jews, “If this matter involved a wrongdoing or vicious crime, O Jews, it would be reasonable for me to hear your complaint.

original.text: μέλλοντος δὲ τοῦ Παύλου ἀνοίγειν τὸ στόμα εἶπεν ὁ Γαλλίων πρὸς τοὺς Ἰουδαίους· Εἰ ⸀μὲν ἦν ἀδίκημά τι ἢ ῥᾳδιούργημα πονηρόν, ὦ Ἰουδαῖοι, κατὰ λόγον ἂν ἀνεσχόμην ὑμῶν·

verses.restored: But if it is questions about a word and names and your own Law, see to it yourselves; I am not willing to be judge of these things.

familiar.text: But if it be a question of words and names, and of your law, look ye to it; for I will be no judge of such matters.

modern.text: But since it is a dispute about words and names and your own law, settle it yourselves. I refuse to be a judge of such things.”

original.text: εἰ δὲ ⸀ζητήματά ἐστιν περὶ λόγου καὶ ὀνομάτων καὶ νόμου τοῦ καθʼ ὑμᾶς, ὄψεσθε αὐτοί· ⸀κριτὴς ἐγὼ τούτων οὐ βούλομαι εἶναι.

verses.restored: He drove them from the judgment seat.

familiar.text: And he drave them from the judgment seat.

modern.text: And he drove them away from the judgment seat.

original.text: καὶ ἀπήλασεν αὐτοὺς ἀπὸ τοῦ βήματος.

verses.restored: They all seized Sosthenes, the synagogue ruler, and beat him before the judgment seat, and none of these things mattered to Gallio.

familiar.text: Then all the Greeks took Sosthenes, the chief ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat. And Gallio cared for none of those things.

modern.text: At this, the crowd seized Sosthenes the synagogue leader and beat him in front of the judgment seat. But none of this was of concern to Gallio. Paul Returns to Antioch

original.text: ἐπιλαβόμενοι δὲ ⸀πάντες Σωσθένην τὸν ἀρχισυνάγωγον ἔτυπτον ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ βήματος· καὶ οὐδὲν τούτων τῷ Γαλλίωνι ⸀ἔμελεν.

verses.restored: Paul, remaining many days longer, said farewell to the siblings and sailed away to Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila. In Cenchreae he cut his hair, for he had a vow.

familiar.text: And Paul after this tarried there yet a good while, and then took his leave of the brethren, and sailed thence into Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquila; having shorn his head in Cenchrea: for he had a vow.

modern.text: Paul remained in Corinth for quite some time before saying goodbye to the brothers. He had his head shaved in Cenchrea to keep a vow he had made, and then he sailed for Syria, accompanied by Priscilla and Aquila.

original.text: Ὁ δὲ Παῦλος ἔτι προσμείνας ἡμέρας ἱκανὰς τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ἀποταξάμενος ἐξέπλει εἰς τὴν Συρίαν, καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ Πρίσκιλλα καὶ Ἀκύλας, κειράμενος ⸂ἐν Κεγχρεαῖς τὴν κεφαλήν⸃, εἶχεν γὰρ εὐχήν.

verses.restored: They came to Ephesus, and he left them there. He himself entered the synagogue and reasoned with the Judeans.

familiar.text: And he came to Ephesus, and left them there: but he himself entered into the synagogue, and reasoned with the Jews.

modern.text: When they reached Ephesus, Paul parted ways with Priscilla and Aquila. He himself went into the synagogue there and reasoned with the Jews.

original.text: ⸀κατήντησαν δὲ εἰς Ἔφεσον, κἀκείνους κατέλιπεν αὐτοῦ, αὐτὸς δὲ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν ⸀διελέξατο τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις.

verses.restored: When they asked him to remain for a longer time, he did not consent,

familiar.text: When they desired him to tarry longer time with them, he consented not;

modern.text: When they asked him to stay for a while longer, he declined.

original.text: ἐρωτώντων δὲ αὐτῶν ἐπὶ πλείονα χρόνον ⸀μεῖναι οὐκ ἐπένευσεν,

verses.restored: but saying farewell and saying, I will return to you again, the Divine willing, he set sail from Ephesus.

familiar.text: But bade them farewell, saying, I must by all means keep this feast that cometh in Jerusalem: but I will return again unto you, if God will. And he sailed from Ephesus.

modern.text: But as he left, he said, “I will come back to you if God is willing.” And he set sail from Ephesus.

original.text: ⸂ἀλλὰ ἀποταξάμενος καὶ⸃ ⸀εἰπών· ⸀Πάλιν ἀνακάμψω πρὸς ὑμᾶς τοῦ θεοῦ θέλοντος ἀνήχθη ἀπὸ τῆς Ἐφέσου,

verses.restored: Coming down to Caesarea, going up and greeting the assembly, he went down to Antioch.

familiar.text: And when he had landed at Caesarea, and gone up, and saluted the church, he went down to Antioch.

modern.text: When Paul had landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the church at Jerusalem. Then he went down to Antioch. Paul’s Third Missionary Journey Begins (Acts 13:1–3; Acts 15:36–41)

original.text: καὶ κατελθὼν εἰς Καισάρειαν, ἀναβὰς καὶ ἀσπασάμενος τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, κατέβη εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν,

verses.restored: After spending some time, he departed, passing through the Galatian region and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.

familiar.text: And after he had spent some time there, he departed, and went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.

modern.text: After Paul had spent some time in Antioch, he traveled from place to place throughout the region of Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the disciples.

original.text: καὶ ποιήσας χρόνον τινὰ ἐξῆλθεν, διερχόμενος καθεξῆς τὴν Γαλατικὴν χώραν καὶ Φρυγίαν, ⸀στηρίζων πάντας τοὺς μαθητάς.

verses.restored: A certain Judean named Apollos, Alexandrian by birth, an eloquent man, powerful in the Scriptures, came to Ephesus.

familiar.text: And a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, and mighty in the scriptures, came to Ephesus.

modern.text: Meanwhile a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria, came to Ephesus. He was an eloquent man, well versed in the Scriptures.

original.text: Ἰουδαῖος δέ τις Ἀπολλῶς ὀνόματι, Ἀλεξανδρεὺς τῷ γένει, ἀνὴρ λόγιος, κατήντησεν εἰς Ἔφεσον, δυνατὸς ὢν ἐν ταῖς γραφαῖς.

verses.restored: This one had been instructed in the Way of the Lord, and being fervent in spirit, he was speaking and teaching accurately the things concerning Jesus, knowing only the baptism of John.

familiar.text: This man was instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in the spirit, he spake and taught diligently the things of the Lord, knowing only the baptism of John.

modern.text: He had been instructed in the way of the Lord and was fervent in spirit. He spoke and taught accurately about Jesus, though he knew only the baptism of John.

original.text: οὗτος ἦν κατηχημένος τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ κυρίου, καὶ ζέων τῷ πνεύματι ἐλάλει καὶ ἐδίδασκεν ἀκριβῶς τὰ περὶ τοῦ ⸀Ἰησοῦ, ἐπιστάμενος μόνον τὸ βάπτισμα Ἰωάννου.

verses.restored: He began to speak boldly in the synagogue. Hearing him, Priscilla and Aquila took him aside and explained to him the Way of the Divine more accurately.

familiar.text: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue: whom when Aquila and Priscilla had heard, they took him unto them, and expounded unto him the way of God more perfectly.

modern.text: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue. When Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him in and explained to him the way of God more accurately.

original.text: οὗτός τε ἤρξατο παρρησιάζεσθαι ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ· ἀκούσαντες δὲ αὐτοῦ ⸂Πρίσκιλλα καὶ Ἀκύλας⸃ προσελάβοντο αὐτὸν καὶ ἀκριβέστερον αὐτῷ ἐξέθεντο τὴν ⸂ὁδὸν τοῦ θεοῦ⸃.

verses.restored: When he wished to pass through to Achaia, the siblings encouraged him and wrote to the disciples to welcome him. Arriving, he greatly helped those who through grace had trusted,

familiar.text: And when he was disposed to pass into Achaia, the brethren wrote, exhorting the disciples to receive him: who, when he was come, helped them much which had believed through grace:

modern.text: When Apollos resolved to cross over to Achaia, the brothers encouraged him and wrote to the disciples there to welcome him. On his arrival, he was a great help to those who by grace had believed.

original.text: βουλομένου δὲ αὐτοῦ διελθεῖν εἰς τὴν Ἀχαΐαν προτρεψάμενοι οἱ ἀδελφοὶ ἔγραψαν τοῖς μαθηταῖς ἀποδέξασθαι αὐτόν· ὃς παραγενόμενος συνεβάλετο πολὺ τοῖς πεπιστευκόσιν διὰ τῆς χάριτος·

verses.restored: for he was powerfully refuting the Judeans publicly, showing through the Scriptures that Jesus is the Messiah.

familiar.text: For he mightily convinced the Jews, and that publickly, shewing by the scriptures that Jesus was Christ.

modern.text: For he powerfully refuted the Jews in public debate, proving from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.

original.text: εὐτόνως γὰρ τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις διακατηλέγχετο δημοσίᾳ ἐπιδεικνὺς διὰ τῶν γραφῶν εἶναι τὸν χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν.
